public_types.adaptation: Existing Rust Invalid/Overflow/Limit/OutOfMemory variants remain frozen; success is represented by Result::Ok rather than a success enum variant.
Borrowed slices encode pointer validity and length together.

allocation_and_slice_adaptation: Safe 4096-aligned fixed blocks preserve supported alignment without unsafe code. Borrowed allocation views are segmented ArenaSlice/ArenaSliceMut objects with byte access and copy methods, since the standard library cannot safely reinterpret aligned-block storage as one contiguous byte slice. Handles carry an arena identity and do not expose addresses. No external dependencies or unsafe code are used.
unrepresentable_c_cases: Null output pointers for arithmetic, subslices, arena construction, and stats have no Rust equivalent; values and Result/Option carry outputs.
Invalid pointer-plus-positive-length byte pairs and invalid null arena arguments cannot be constructed through borrowed slices and owned Arena methods.
Mismatched allocator callback pairs have no counterpart because allocator callbacks are replaced by a typed AllocationGate.
C arena construction can fail while allocating the arena object; Rust Arena construction is an owned value and does not allocate. AllocationGate failure is tested on the first backing chunk instead.

Exact custom allocator allocation/free callback counters have no Rust counterpart. Vec backing allocations are fallible and released by ownership/drop; tests assert failure atomicity and retained handle readability instead.
